clue.text: Royal sultanate has nothing against royal family

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for royal, as in RN or RA
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula
O is the figure zero, nothing
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A royal sultanate holds nothing against a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romanovs were the dynasty that ruled Russia until 1917, a royal (imperial) family.

clue.text: Skint, having lost capital through painting 4

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word for skint is dropped

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money, broke
by can mean through, as in 'by means of'

explanation.surface: Someone penniless loses their capital by way of a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost capital' removes B, the first letter of BROKE, leaving ROKE. 4 is VENUS, so the definition is the Rokeby Venus, Velázquez's painting in the National Gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rokeby Venus is Velázquez's famous nude, named after Rokeby Park where it once hung.

clue.text: Half time — you nearly made it!

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned or put together tells us to reform these letters
nearly means the word you stops short of its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: At half-time a supporter consoles a player who almost scored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half time' looks like a phrase to split into TI or ME, but 'Half' is the definition; 'made' rearranges the time letters plus YO, and 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is a formal or legal word for one of two equal parts, a half share.

clue.text: Eager to embrace quarrel with some elders all about tattooing, say

indicators.note: all about says the whole assembled string is turned round end to end
to embrace means the word for eager holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: eager means keen
a row is a quarrel
some of elders, its first three letters, an old word for age itself

explanation.surface: Someone keen to pick a fight with the church elders over body art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' builds KROWELDEEN, which 'all about' turns end to end; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattooing is an example of work done with a needle, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Body of little beauty after 19

definitions.meaning: a planet is a heavenly body, the second from the Sun
following the word pocket, it makes a phrase for a small, beautiful woman

explanation.walkthrough: 19 is POCKET, and a 'pocket Venus' is an old phrase for a petite beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The second planet from the Sun is a heavenly body, and the goddess of love gives the petite-beauty phrase.

clue.text: Gesture deriding the Queen needs six 19s

parts.note: to cock a snook is a derisive gesture, thumb to nose
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A rude gesture mocking the monarch calls for six pockets of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is POCKET: the cue game played on a table with six pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooker table has six pockets, so the game literally requires them.

clue.text: Setter out about to compete with wiper

indicators.note: about means going around the other piece, so it sits inside
out in the sense of disordered or not in place tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler goes out ready to take on a windscreen wiper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler, but it is just fodder; 'out' and 'about' work together to wrap the vying letters in the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette is a table napkin, used to wipe the mouth and fingers.

clue.text: Emperor with foothold out of crease

indicators.note: out of tells us the letters of one word are taken away from the other

parts.note: a fold is a crease

explanation.surface: A ruler gains a foothold after escaping a cricket crease.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing F, O, L and D, in order, from FOOTHOLD leaves the emperor. The 'crease' looks like a cricket reference but is just FOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Otho was a Roman emperor who ruled briefly in AD 69, the Year of the Four Emperors.

clue.text: Cover for head, right cheek if needed, or 21 for 19

indicators.note: needed sounds like kneaded, worked like dough, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A head covering, worn on the right cheek if necessary, or tucked in a hand pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or 21 for 19' adds a second hint: put HAND (21) in front and you get a handkerchief, which goes in a POCKET (19).
explanation.definitionFit: A kerchief is a cloth square worn over the head or tied round it.

clue.text: Painter only worked in colours

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for colours

parts.note: reds are colours

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded into a different form

explanation.surface: An artist who used only bright paints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' makes YNOL, and 'in' places it inside the colours word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joshua Reynolds was the leading English portrait painter of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Some said "an eye for an eye" after 19

indicators.note: said means the extracted run is spoken, and it sounds like a word
some means only part of the quoted phrase is used, here a run from its start

explanation.surface: Some quote the biblical rule of retribution following a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Part of 'an eye for' is N-EYE-F, which spoken sounds like the answer. The definition is 'after 19': the word that follows POCKET in a familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket knife is a folding blade carried in the pocket, so the word comes after POCKET.

clue.text: Coming from the Pole — that or the railway?

parts.note: that points back to the Pole, the north one, abbreviated N
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is that traveller coming from the Arctic, or from the train?
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' refers back to the Pole in the definition, which here is the North Pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A northerly wind blows from the north, so it comes from the direction of the North Pole.

clue.text: 15 — or should it be Queen? — maybe 19

definitions.text: 15 — or should it be Queen? — maybe 19

parts.words: 15 — or should it be Queen? — maybe 19
parts.note: a warship of His or Her Majesty's navy is a king's craft or, under a queen, the queen's; a small version of it was the pocket kind

explanation.walkthrough: 15 is KINGCRAFT, read here as 'king's craft', a Royal Navy ship; 19 is POCKET, and a pocket battleship was a small German warship of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleship is a heavily armed warship, and the pocket variety was a smaller class of it.

clue.text: Go away to get in with no contest

definitions.meaning: an exclamation telling someone or something to leave

definitions.text: to get in with no contest
definitions.meaning: add in and you get the phrase for a certain winner, one who faces no real contest

explanation.walkthrough: A 'shoo-in' is a candidate certain to win, originally American racing slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is an exclamation driving away birds or animals, an order to leave.

clue.text: Most of 7 19 watch one after talent

parts.note: 7 is the kerchief entry; most of it is its last five letters, a word meaning boss or leader, which gives a synonym for that
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged metal cover over the face

explanation.surface: A recruiter looks most of the time at their pocket watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of KERCHIEF is CHIEF, which means HEAD. 19 is POCKET, and a hunter is a kind of pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A headhunter is a recruiter who seeks out talented people for senior jobs.

clue.text: Make a noise like the last trump

definitions.text: Make a noise like the last trump

parts.words: Make a noise like the last trump
parts.note: the trumpet of Judgment Day will raise those in their graves, so any loud enough din is likened to it

explanation.walkthrough: The 'last trump' is the trumpet call on Judgment Day that raises the dead, so it is not a card game reference.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a deafening racket is idiomatically said to be loud enough to rouse corpses from their graves.

clue.text: Machiavelli's subject, like corruption, includes its leader

parts.note: kin means related, alike

indicators.note: includes means the word for corruption holds a letter inside it

parts.note: graft is corruption, bribery for gain
its leader is the first letter of corruption, C

explanation.surface: A Renaissance writer's theme, as corruption includes its own leader.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAFT takes in C after its G to give GCRAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingcraft is the art of ruling, the theme of Machiavelli's The Prince.

clue.text: Surfaces roads — so Cleopatra doesn't get bitten?

definitions.meaning: lays a tarmac-like coating over road surfaces
read as two words, the snake stops, so the queen escapes her famous fatal bite

explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra is said to have died from the bite of an asp, an Egyptian snake.
explanation.definitionFit: To asphalt a road is to coat it with bitumen mix, so the verb means surfaces.

clue.text: Work to give power, having a key

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to enable is to give power or means

explanation.surface: A job meant to empower someone has a key to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has a key can be unlocked and so is capable of being opened.

clue.text: Be a top copper, more than usually mean?

parts.note: super as a prefix means above or beyond the usual
to mean is to intend

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is asked whether they are especially stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy, but here it is the verb, intend.
explanation.definitionFit: To superintend is to oversee, and a superintendent is a senior police rank, so it plays on the title.

clue.text: See 23
One taking interest in turn for having extra security

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for turn
surer means more secure, having extra security

explanation.surface: A lender takes an interest in exchange for more collateral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' looks like curiosity but is money charged on a loan; 'in' and 'for having' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money and charges interest, usually at an excessive rate.

clue.text: Carefully select worker to take from 19

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
19 is pocket; a pickpocket takes from pockets, so to pick is to steal from one

explanation.surface: A labourer picks pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: To handpick is to choose personally and with care.

clue.text: Diseased flour cooked and eaten by Liverpudlian missing drug

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside the other piece
missing means the drug letter is left out

parts.note: a Scouse is a native of Liverpool
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad flour is baked and eaten by someone from Liverpool who is short of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' leaves SCOUS, and 'cooked' makes ROFUL, which 'eaten by' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrofulous means affected by scrofula, a tubercular disease of the neck glands.

clue.text: Took up English football club to effect losing money

indicators.note: to effect is to bring about or produce, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: FC is football club

explanation.surface: A football club is taken over and pushed into financial loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TOOK UP, E, FC and TO are rearranged by 'effect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of pocket means having lost money, typically through expenses.

clue.text: See 21
Missing lord keeping some British model smoother

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within

parts.note: Lord Lucan vanished in 1974 and was never found
some of British, its first three letters, gives a short piece of it
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A disappeared aristocrat is holding a British model of a smoother.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Lucan is a British peer who vanished in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered; 'keeping' places the short British piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lubricant is an oil or grease that reduces friction, so it is something that smooths.

clue.text: One willing to bet at a 7, in part

indicators.note: in part means only a piece of the words is taken, here a run across them

explanation.surface: A gambler in a headscarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is KERCHIEF, so 'at a 7' becomes AT A KERCHIEF, and the run is in aT A KERchief.
explanation.definitionFit: A taker is someone who accepts a bet or offer, as in 'any takers?'.

clue.text: General in burlesque resembling a mouse?

indicators.note: in places the general inside the word for burlesque

parts.note: a skit is a burlesque, a comic parody
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A general appears in a comic sketch looking timid and mousy.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns's poem 'To a Mouse' opens 'Wee, sleekit, cow'rin, tim'rous beastie', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleekit is a Scots word meaning sleek and smooth, famously applied to a mouse by Burns.

clue.text: Carer finally comes in to nurse novelist

indicators.note: comes in means the letter is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: to foster is to nurse or bring up

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of carer

explanation.surface: A carer finally arrives to nurse a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: E M Forster wrote A Passage to India and Howards End.
